input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: Section 17(b) gives us (Sparkling) an unqualified right to terminate for convenience at any time on ninety (90) days' written notice, and no early-termination fee or penalty is imposed anywhere (Section 11 and the Fee Schedule reference no exit charge). Garman has no corresponding convenience right: its only termination rights arise under Section 17(c) on insolvency or uncured material default, which satisfies the preferred position that the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term. The clause therefore sits at the fallback on notice period (60–90 days rather than the preferred 30 days) and better than fallback on fees, so it is compliant and we do not redline it. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted only: the 90-day notice is at the outer edge of the fallback range, and Section 17(b) contains no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (refund of fees for services not yet rendered is expressly provided only on termination for Garman's default under Section 17(c)). If the agreement is reopened for other reasons, we would seek 30 days' notice and an express pro-rata refund.
